title: The Far Trail
premise: Wendell Montrose, a storm chaser drowning in debt to the Meridian Fund—a crew of cheerful, ruthless lenders—takes a salvage contract to recover equipment left behind by a vanished government survey team in the Redwater Basin. With his ragtag crew of misfits who have become his only real family, Wendell discovers the surveyors didn't vanish: they found something at the river's forbidden source that powerful people will kill to keep buried. Racing the dry season upstream through canyon country, pursued by both the Fund's collectors and government fixers, Wendell must choose between paying his debts and exposing the truth. In the end, he burns his own escape route to carry the evidence out, loses the money that defined him, and gains something worth more: a family bound by choice and a justice the law was never going to deliver.
about_author: Paloma Voss is a former backcountry guide who spent six seasons leading expeditions through remote river canyons before turning to fiction full-time. She writes adventure stories about people rebuilding themselves far from anywhere with cell service.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Introduces Wendell chasing a supercell across the plains while dodging calls from the Meridian Fund, establishing his debt, his truck, and his philosophy of measuring life in miles. Emotional beat: restless avoidance—he's running from numbers he can't outrun.

chapters.title: The Optimists
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A meeting with the Meridian Fund's smiling enforcer, Corliss Ames, who offers him a way out: salvage the vanished survey team's gear from the Redwater Basin. Beat: dread dressed as opportunity; Wendell signs because he sees no other door.

chapters.title: Crew of Strays
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV as he gathers his team: Junie, a navigator who reads water like text; Bo, an ex-paramedic with a suspended license; and Teo, a teenage drone pilot fleeing a custody battle. Beat: warmth—the found family assembling, each carrying a wound.

chapters.title: Gear and No Tracks
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. The crew reaches the abandoned survey camp: tents intact, instruments still recording, meals half-eaten—but no footprints leaving. Beat: uncanny unease; the first hint this is no ordinary disappearance.

chapters.title: What the Instruments Saw
chapters.summary: Teo's POV. Recovering the data drives, Teo finds the survey team's final logs: readings of something vast and moving beneath the river's headwaters, followed by a deliberate shutdown. Beat: curiosity curdling into fear.

chapters.title: The Second Party
chapters.summary: Bo's POV. A second group arrives at the camp—government 'fixers' led by the cold, methodical Agent Reyes—who claim jurisdiction and order them out. Beat: menace; Wendell realizes the Fund and the government are circling the same secret.

chapters.title: Upstream
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. Defying the eviction, the crew slips upriver at night into the closed basin, following the survey team's route toward the source before the dry season drops the water levels. Beat: commitment—the point of no return, exhilarating and terrifying.

chapters.title: The Narrows
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A whitewater passage nearly kills them; Bo saves Teo from a flip, cementing the crew's trust. They find the survey team's second cache and a journal page: 'It isn't geology.' Beat: bonding forged in danger.

chapters.title: Corliss on the Radio
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Ames contacts them via satellite phone: recover the source data or the debt doubles and the crew becomes liable too. Beat: pressure tightening; Wendell hides the threat from the others, repeating old patterns of solitary burden.

chapters.title: Dry Season
chapters.summary: Teo's POV. The river shrinks, forcing them to portage through heat and dust; supplies dwindle and tempers fray. Junie confronts Wendell about the call she overheard. Beat: fracture—the family strains under secrets.

chapters.title: The Surveyor's Grave
chapters.summary: Bo's POV. They find one surveyor, dead not from accident but execution, and buried with care by his teammates. His notebook names what they found: an unregistered aquifer feeding three states—and the deal to sell it secretly. Beat: grief and moral clarity; the stakes become human.

chapters.title: Reyes Closes In
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. The fixers' helicopter passes overhead; the crew hides in a slot canyon as Reyes's team ransacks their abandoned rafts. Beat: hunted-animal tension; they understand they're witnesses marked for erasure.

chapters.title: The Fork
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. At a canyon fork, the crew votes: abandon the source and run for the border of the basin, or push on. Teo casts the deciding vote for truth. Beat: agency reclaimed—the family chooses its own justice over survival alone.

chapters.title: Ames Arrives
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The Fund's collectors intercept them on foot; Ames offers Wendell a personal out if he surrenders the data drives and abandons the crew. Beat: temptation and refusal—Wendell, for the first time, chooses people over the ledger.

chapters.title: Blood in the Shallows
chapters.summary: Bo's POV. A violent standoff in the shallows leaves Bo wounded shielding Teo; the crew scatters the collectors' boats and flees upstream bleeding but together. Beat: sacrifice—the found family proves it will bleed for each other.

chapters.title: The Source
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. They reach the forbidden source: a cathedral cavern where the river rises from a hidden aquifer, and the surviving surveyors—three of them, hiding for months—are waiting. Beat: awe and revelation; the mystery resolves into conspiracy.

chapters.title: Witnesses
chapters.summary: Surveyor Elena Marsh's POV (interleaved with Wendell's). The survivors tell their story: they refused to falsify findings, were disavowed, and have been surviving on cave water waiting for someone honest to arrive. Beat: vindication and shared purpose.

chapters.title: Reyes at the Door
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Reyes's team storms the cavern; a standoff in the dark ends when Teo broadcasts the aquifer data and the execution evidence to every news outlet and water authority in the region. Beat: climax—truth as a weapon fired at last.

chapters.title: The Long Way Down
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. With the story public, Reyes withdraws rather than become the headline; the crew guides the injured survivors downriver as the dry season finally closes the upper canyon behind them. Beat: exhale—escape transformed into escort, danger receding.

chapters.title: Settling Accounts
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell faces Ames with nothing left to seize: the debt voided by exposure of the Fund's ties to the water deal, Ames walking away with empty hands and a smile gone thin. Beat: liberation—Wendell is free precisely because he has nothing left to lose.

chapters.title: Names on a Map
chapters.summary: Teo's POV. Weeks later: congressional hearings begin, the surveyors are honored, and Teo's custody case resolves with the crew testifying as character witnesses. Beat: restoration—justice inside the law at last, built on the justice they made outside it.

chapters.title: The Far Trail
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The crew loads a new truck for a season of storm chasing with no contracts and no debts, Wendell finally measuring life in years and the people filling them. Final beat: home—not a place, but the family riding beside him, the road open ahead.
